requirement:
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures` has one core obligation. `Criterion::execute` can compute an answer directly from tracked inputs with no configured model provider or agent. I did not read the implementation source. I judged the tests from their assertions.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[deterministic_validation_uses_required_storage_without_an_agent]` is the main test. It uses a `Memory` graph with no agent. It first asserts that `ValidationContext::ask::<bool>()` returns `NoAgentConfigured`, which shows that no agent is present. It then runs `validator.verify(Review(..))` on a deterministic criterion and unwraps the result, so execution succeeds without an agent. It asserts the computed output: `result` is false and `rationale` is "ordinary computation". It stores the evidence, loads it back, and asserts that the dependency is `Dependency::Node(Node(1), fingerprint)` with the expected fingerprint. That covers computing the answer from tracked inputs.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` covers the case where an agent is configured but unusable. The `ValidationCache` has an OpenAI config whose credential env var does not exist. The deterministic `Question(false, ..)` still refreshes successfully. It returns output false with one dependency, so deterministic execution does not touch the provider. The agent-asking `Question(true, ..)` fails with `ValidationError::Provider`. This contrast shows that deterministic execution needs no working agent.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[caller_reuses_negative_answers_and_compares_revisions_explicitly]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` add further coverage. In both, plain domains with no agent execute criteria directly. They assert the typed outputs and the recorded dependencies, and that only an explicit store writes anything. The `Memory` test asserts the recorded dependencies are empty and that there were no reads or selections. The `contracts.rs` test asserts that `state.reads` is empty and that all records have no dependencies. Neither test conflicts with the requirement.

I found no uncovered obligation, boundary or failure case, and I found no missing `{test}` references.
